app: WordPress 7.1.4 (upstream image) + WooCommerce 11.2.2 (official plugin zip, sha256 a4746183...) + MariaDB 11.8.9, all unmodified
generic_extensions_used: writable paths owned by the service uid (mode 0755)
allow-listed namespaced sysctl (net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start) so non-root Apache binds :80 with no capabilities
setup steps: wp-cli exec, SQL user creation, header captures (Store API Nonce, Cart-Token), add-to-cart
'set' step for a per-run scope value
fabricated response rendered with job variables

app_specific_workarounds.what: plugin installed by wp-cli from the official zip mounted read-only outside the web root
app_specific_workarounds.why: mounting the plugin directory inside the web root made Docker create root-owned mountpoints that broke WordPress's own file copy
with WordPress's default plain permalinks, POST /wp-json/... is not routed and returns the HOME PAGE with HTTP 200 (a silent no-op that looks like success)

app_specific_workarounds.what: store options via wp-cli (coming-soon off, cash-on-delivery on) and a product created with wp-cli
app_specific_workarounds.kind: seed data via the app's own CLI

native_duplicate_prevention.evidence: AM-2 probe: lost_ack applied (503, committed); the identical resubmission got 409 woocommerce_rest_cart_empty; verified effects stay 1. Self-test G2 and G3b fail for this reason; G1, G3a and G4 pass and proxy-inferred == verified in every case
native_duplicate_prevention.harness_result: NOT ASSESSED (correct under the protocol: the positive control cannot produce a duplicate by identical resubmission)
native_duplicate_prevention.caveat: an agent that RE-ADDS the item and checks out again could still create a second order; the protocol's positive control (identical resubmission) does not model that

browser_D6.lost_ack: WooCommerce's own error 'Something went wrong...' AND 'Your cart is currently empty' (the order was placed); verified 1
browser_D6.delayed_commit: same error with the cart still full; verified 0 then 1 after the delay
browser_D6.fabricated: the UI followed the success response to WooCommerce's real order-received page ('Please check your email for the order confirmation'); verified 0
browser_D6.level: B2: worked with the proxy as it was (after the Vikunja/Gitea fixes), email-based scope matched the UI's checkout request; supporting cart writes (/batch 207) classified

fidelity_D2.fabricated: F1 (the most convincing of the four apps: the app's own success page, but a generic one)

AM5.native_idempotency_keys: none for Store API checkout; duplicates are prevented by cart state, not keys

AM6_exploratory.pre_commit_failure: feasible F2 by analysis (same checkout error path)
AM6_exploratory.stale_read: feasible F1 for Store API cart reads
